kaps_punt: Berge, bergreekse, valleie en heuwels, riviere, watervalle, kuslyne - kape en baaie (hier net berge, bergreekse en heuwels); Ligging van belangrike fisiese verskynsels in eie provinsie; Ligging van geselekteerde fisiese verskynsels in Suid-Afrika - soos Tafelberg, the uKhahlamba-Drakensberg, Waterberg (kaart)

items.bewering: 'n Berg is land wat hoog en steil bo sy omgewing uitstaan.
items.bron: National Geographic Education 'Mountain' / 'Hill' (education.nationalgeographic.org): a mountain rises prominently above its surroundings with steep slopes; hills are less steep and not as high.

items.bewering: Berge staan dikwels saam in 'n lang ry. So 'n ry berge wat aanmekaar lê, is 'n bergreeks.
items.bron: National Geographic: a mountain range is a series or chain of mountains close together; Wikipedia 'Mountain range': a series of mountains arranged in a line and connected by high ground.

items.bewering: 'n Heuwel is laer en ronder as 'n berg.
items.bron: National Geographic Education 'Hill': a hill is lower and less steep than a mountain, generally with a rounded top.

items.bewering: Daar is geen vaste hoogte waar 'n heuwel 'n berg word nie.
items.bron: National Geographic Education 'Hill' and USGS FAQ 'What is the difference between a lake and a pond; a mountain and a hill...': no official definitions; the old 1 000-foot convention was abandoned.

Wikipedia 'Drakensberg': the escarpment stretches for more than 1 000 km; South African Tourism 'uKhahlamba / Drakensberg' (saspecialist.southafrica.net): in Zulu the range is known as uKhahlamba, 'barrier of spears'. Note: Wikipedia applies uKhahlamba strictly to the highest portion, SA Tourism to the whole range; the lesson uses the compound name for the range and plain 'Drakensberg' for its full extent, which is consistent with both.

items.bewering: Dit is deel van die eskarp, die steil rand van die binnelandse plato.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Drakensberg': the eastern portion of the Great Escarpment, which encloses the central Southern African plateau.

items.bewering: Die Drakensberg strek van die Oos-Kaap deur KwaZulu-Natal en die Vrystaat tot in Mpumalanga en Limpopo.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Drakensberg': from the Eastern Cape in the south, along the Lesotho border, then as the border between KwaZulu-Natal and the Free State and Mpumalanga, through Mpumalanga, and 'farther north to Hoedspruit in southeastern Limpopo'.

items.bewering: Sy hoogste deel lê langs die grens tussen KwaZulu-Natal en Lesotho.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Drakensberg' (the highest peaks are all in the area bordering on Lesotho, where the escarpment forms the Lesotho-KwaZulu-Natal border); Wikipedia 'List of mountains in South Africa': Mafadi, 3 450 m, highest point in South Africa, on the border; Thabana Ntlenyana, 3 482 m, on the Drakensberg ridge just inside Lesotho near Sani Pass. The 'highest part' is correctly placed along the border; the lesson does not claim the highest peak is in South Africa.

items.bewering: Tafelberg staan bo Kaapstad in die Wes-Kaap.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Table Mountain'; City of Cape Town 'Cape Town's mountains' (capetown.gov.za).

items.bewering: Sy steil kante styg hoog bo die stad uit.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Table Mountain': flat-topped plateau edged by steep cliffs, highest point about 1 085 m at Maclear's Beacon, forming the backdrop to Cape Town.

items.bewering: Die bokant van die berg is amper so plat soos 'n tafel.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Table Mountain': a level plateau about 3 km side to side, a resistant sandstone cap left as a long level table. Mapping holds: the comparison is to flatness only, and 'amper' correctly allows for the uneven back table and Maclear's Beacon; a learner reasoning further (flat top, steep sides) is led to the right picture.

items.bewering: Die Waterberg lê ver in die noorde, in Limpopo.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Waterberg Massif' / 'Waterberg Biosphere' (sandstone massif in north Limpopo; UNESCO biosphere reserve since 2001); University of Pretoria thesis on the Waterberg (repository.up.ac.za).

items.bewering: Dit is 'n groot berggebied met hoë kranse en riviere.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Waterberg Massif': sandstone plateaus and escarpments with bluffs and buttes from river erosion, peaks to about 2 000 m; University of Pretoria thesis: drained by the Lephalala, Mokolo, Matlabas and Mogalakwena rivers; biosphere reserve of several hundred thousand hectares.

items.bewering: Jy kan die fisiese verskynsels in jou eie provinsie op 'n fisiese kaart vind. ... Kyk dan na die sleutel se kleure vir hoë en lae land.
items.bron: Natural Earth 'Cross-blended Hypsometric Tints' and Ask About Ireland 'Using different colours to show height': physical maps show elevation with layer tints explained in the key (conventionally green low, brown high), and the map's own key governs.

items.bewering: die uKhahlamba-Drakensberg as 'n lang bergreeks van die Oos-Kaap deur KwaZulu-Natal en die Vrystaat tot in Mpumalanga en Limpopo, met sy hoogste deel langs die grens tussen KwaZulu-Natal en Lesotho; en die Waterberg in Limpopo; Tafelberg bo Kaapstad in die Wes-Kaap
items.bron: Same as the study-block items above: Wikipedia 'Drakensberg' (extent, highest part), South African Tourism 'uKhahlamba / Drakensberg' (name for the range), Wikipedia 'Waterberg Massif', Wikipedia 'Table Mountain'.

items.bewering: berg: Land wat hoog en steil bo sy omgewing uitstaan.
bergreeks: 'n Ry berge wat aanmekaar lê, soos die uKhahlamba-Drakensberg.
items.bron: National Geographic and Wikipedia 'Mountain range' (definition); Wikipedia 'Drakensberg' (a 1 000 km range, the example is apt).

items.bewering: heuwel: Land wat bo sy omgewing uitstaan maar laer en ronder as 'n berg is.
eskarp: Die steil rand waar die plato na laer land toe afloop.
items.bron: Unisa GeoTerm 'escarpment' (gama.unisa.ac.za/geoterm/concepts/115/en); Wikipedia 'Great Escarpment, Southern Africa'.

opsomming: Every claim in this lesson was checked and holds, including where the Drakensberg runs and that its highest part lies along the KwaZulu-Natal-Lesotho border; the only point worth a person knowing is that sources differ on whether the Zulu name uKhahlamba covers the whole range or only its highest part, and the lesson's wording is consistent with both.
